advanced-industries.overview: Advanced industries covers engineering-heavy manufacturers: carmakers and their suppliers, aircraft and defense companies, and makers of industrial machinery and equipment. Products take years to design and depend on long, global supply chains, so these companies are shaped by how full their factories are, trade policy and the cost of materials like steel. A large share of their profit often comes from servicing and spare parts after the original sale.
advanced-industries.recap: Data center demand and defense orders drove results. Vertiv's sales jumped 61% and orders more than doubled, and Caterpillar's sales rose 17% to $20.7 billion with data center power generation up 30%. General Dynamics' backlog rose to $220 billion after $94 billion of submarine-led orders, and Boeing reported a record $745 billion backlog despite a quarterly loss. Ford raised the low end of its 2026 profit outlook to $10.5 to $11 billion while its electric vehicles still lose about $4 billion, and Rivian's revenue rose 38% to $2.16 billion.

consumer-retail.overview: Consumer and retail covers the companies that make and sell what people buy day to day. That includes stores and online retailers, makers of food, drinks and household products, farm and food businesses, and travel and hospitality companies like airlines and hotels. Consumer spending is about two-thirds of the US economy, so these businesses rise and fall with how confident people feel and how much money they have left after essentials.
consumer-retail.recap: Delivery and restaurants led the news. DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for about $17 billion, Starbucks reported same-store sales up 7.2%, and Restaurant Brands said Burger King US comparable sales rose 8.4% while Popeyes fell 1.8%. Coca-Cola raised its 2026 outlook on 7% organic revenue growth. Weaker names stood out: Whirlpool swung to a $249 million quarterly loss and skipped its dividend, and a Trian-led group proposed a $7.35-a-share cash buyout of Wendy's, a 20% premium.

energy-materials.overview: Energy and materials covers the companies that pull resources out of the ground and turn them into fuel, power and raw materials. That includes oil and gas producers, the pipelines, ships and terminals that move their output, refineries and chemical plants, electric utilities and renewable developers, and miners and steelmakers. These are capital-heavy businesses that live with commodity prices they don't control, so returns depend on keeping costs low and investing at the right point in the cycle.
energy-materials.recap: Oil ended October sharply higher: Brent gained 13.6% on attacks on Saudi sites and a tanker mine strike in Hormuz, its highest since April, and Brent traded near $112 to $115 on Friday. Refining margins carried the big producers: Exxon's adjusted profit rose to $17.5 billion, Chevron nearly tripled its profit to $9.9 billion and plans a $7 billion Venezuela investment, and Shell's adjusted earnings doubled to $10.8 billion. Dealmaking continued with EQT buying Range Resources, Ovintiv buying Logan Energy for about $890 million and GE Vernova buying grid-equipment maker Trench for $9 billion. Gas-engine maker INNIO raised guidance on 57% revenue growth, while Enphase guided to weaker US residential solar demand.

financial-services.overview: Financial services is the business of managing, lending, investing and moving money. Banks take deposits and make loans, insurers collect premiums to cover risks, asset managers invest on behalf of savers and pension funds, and payments companies handle the flow of money between people and businesses. It is one of the most heavily regulated industries, so how much capital firms must hold and how well they control risk shapes how profitable they can be.
financial-services.recap: Payments and banks reported strong quarters. American Express posted record revenue of $20.1 billion but announced a 5% job cut, Visa ended its fiscal year with $45.9 billion in revenue, up 15%, and Mastercard's net revenue rose 14% to $9.8 billion with cross-border volume up 11%. HSBC's third-quarter pre-tax profit rose 32% to $9.6 billion, helped by a legal charge from a year earlier not repeating. Deals focused on trading and credit: Tradeweb agreed to buy Trumid for about $1.97 billion, Ares Capital agreed to buy MidCap Financial for about $2.6 billion, and Markel moved $2.3 billion of old reinsurance claims to Enstar.

healthcare.overview: Healthcare covers the companies that discover, make, pay for and deliver medical care. Drugmakers and biotech firms develop medicines, device makers build everything from surgical tools to heart implants, insurers pay for care, and hospitals and doctors provide it. In the US the system is large and complex, and prices are set through negotiation between manufacturers, insurers and the middlemen between them, so policy and regulation matter as much as science.
healthcare.recap: Large drugmakers kept growing. Eli Lilly's revenue jumped 39% to $24.4 billion and it raised its 2026 sales outlook to $91 to $92 billion, Merck's Keytruda sales reached $8.6 billion, and Bristol Myers Squibb raised its sales outlook as Eliquis grew 25% but cut earnings guidance on deal charges. AstraZeneca's cancer sales grew 18% and lifted nine-month revenue to $46.9 billion, while older heart and diabetes drugs shrank. Deals focused on care and tools: EQT agreed to take QIAGEN private for $12.1 billion and Bon Secours Mercy Health agreed to buy Surgery Partners for $5.7 billion.

infrastructure-logistics.overview: Infrastructure and logistics covers the physical networks the rest of the economy runs on. That includes the trucking, rail, shipping and air freight companies that move goods, the developers and builders behind homes, offices and data centers, and the public sector that funds and regulates much of it. These businesses are sensitive to fuel costs and interest rates, because moving goods burns diesel and most buildings are paid for with borrowed money.
infrastructure-logistics.recap: Freight and deals defined the week. UPS beat estimates and lifted its 2026 outlook as it winds down Amazon volume, and Landstar's revenue rose 25% to $1.51 billion on higher truck rates, although claims costs cut its profit. Maximus agreed to buy defense contractor Agile Defense for $660 million. Thrive Holdings agreed to take home-security company ADT private in a deal valued at $15.3 billion including debt, financed by Apollo funds, with a go-shop period running to November 28.

macro.overview: The macro picture covers the forces that move every industry at once: how fast economies are growing, how quickly prices are rising, where central banks set interest rates, and how goods and money flow between countries. When energy costs climb or borrowing gets more expensive, the effects show up in nearly every company's results, so this is the backdrop for reading the rest of the news.
macro.recap: The Fed held at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with two officials wanting a hike, and markets lean toward an increase in December. The economy grew 3.4% in the third quarter while September inflation held at 3.6%. The 10-year Treasury yield sat near 4.93% on Friday after reaching 5.00% a week earlier. Stocks ended the week in a sell-off, with the Nasdaq down 5.3% in October, its worst month since March 2025, as doubts about AI spending spread. This week brings midterm elections on Tuesday and the jobs report on Friday, with forecasts of about 55,000 new jobs.

tmt.overview: Tech, media and telecom covers the companies behind computing and communication: chipmakers, software and cloud providers, internet platforms like search and social media, entertainment and streaming companies, and the telecom networks that connect everything. Many of these businesses become more profitable as they grow, because serving one more customer costs very little, which is why a handful of very large companies dominate. Much of the sector's investment today is going into the data centers and chips that power AI.
tmt.recap: AI spending dominated tech. Microsoft's Azure grew 48% and AWS grew 39% to $46.0 billion, but Alphabet fell 12% in a day and Amazon's free cash flow turned negative as capital spending soared. Intel's server chip revenue rose 78%, yet it fell about 29% on Friday after a weak fourth-quarter forecast, and a semiconductor ETF lost more than 8%. SK hynix earned an 80% operating margin and said the memory shortage will last until 2030, while Reddit and Fortinet shares plunged on weak outlooks. On the deal side, Anthropic filed publicly for a Nasdaq IPO, Guidewire agreed to buy hyperexponential for $1.7 billion and Applied Materials moved to lift its stake in Besi to about 20%.

transport-logistics.overview: Transport and logistics moves goods and people through trucks, trains, ships, planes, warehouses and the brokers that arrange them. It is built from asset-heavy carriers that own vehicles and asset-light intermediaries that sell capacity they do not own. Money is made by keeping assets full and by charging for reliability, with fuel, freight cycles and chokepoints driving the swings. The industry is currently shaped by shipping detours, high fuel costs and large container-ship orderbooks.

travel-hospitality.overview: Travel and hospitality covers the airlines, hotels, cruise lines, booking sites and restaurants that move, host and feed people on trips. Most of the cost is fixed (planes, buildings, crews), so profit swings sharply with how full the seats and rooms are.
